subject: Follow-up: data handling, residency, and support access requirements for Skyline Health
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Daniel Reed <daniel.reed@skylinehealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2026 15:08:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: data handling, residency, and support access requirements for Skyline Health

Hi Daniel / Lena —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and a few targeted clarifying items so we can scope the MPA / security appendix:

- High-level ask from your side: ensure PII never leaves designated residency, define retention windows for transcripts and embeddings, and limit production support staff access to least-privilege with an auditable break-glass flow.
- We attached a privacy matrix (redwood-privacy-matrix.pdf) and a draft timeline (skyline-ma-timeline.xlsx) for the legal + security handoffs.

Clarifying questions so we can finalize the proposal:
1) Residency: are you requiring US-only (multi-region within us-east/us-west) or a specific state-level hosting requirement?
2) Retention: for model logs + transcripts do you want a strict 30/90/365 day policy per data class, or a per-feature retention (e.g., ingestion logs 30d, conversation transcripts 90d, embeddings 365d)?
3) Support access: do you require break-glass to trigger a formal request (Jira ticket + 2x approvers) or is an automated emergency flow with post-hoc audit acceptable?

Proposed next steps:
- Aditya (sec) to confirm auditable break-glass flows and encryption/KMS approach.
- Monica (solutions) to map the RBAC roles to Skyline personas and produce a minimal-permissions matrix.
- We’ll incorporate your answers into the MPA appendix and send an updated DocuSign for signature.

If it helps, I can put together a one-page diagram showing residency + support access flow for your security team.

Thanks —
Irene Choi
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
---
Attachments: redwood-privacy-matrix.pdf (application/pdf, 245KB), skyline-ma-timeline.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 18KB)

From: Daniel Reed <daniel.reed@skylinehealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Lena Park <lena.park@skylinehealth.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2026 18:31:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: data handling, residency, and support access requirements for Skyline Health

Irene — thanks for the summary and the files. A few items to clarify from our security/compliance side:

- Residency: US-only is fine for now, but we need guarantees that data for our patients in CA remains seeded to us-west-2. Do you support pinning by region for live traffic?
- Retention: proposal: transcripts 90 days by default, embeddings treated as derivative material — retention capped at 180 days unless explicitly extended via contract. Audit logs must be retained 1 year.
- Support access: we require a break-glass process that includes an emergency access ticket (Jira SUP-421) + a secondary approver in our security team. Post-access, we need a full session recording and the exact API calls made by support.

Also: are you SOC 2 + HIPAA supportive? We need the specific shadowing controls for support engineers (no ad-hoc shell access).

Happy to jump on a quick follow-up with Aditya and Monica next week — Wed or Thu morning PST works for us.

Best,
Daniel Reed
Director, Platform Security | Skyline Health

On Sat, Dec 12, 2026 at 15:08, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com> wrote:

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 13 Dec 2026 09:14:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: data handling, residency, and support access requirements for Skyline Health (internal)

Irene / Monica — quick internal notes following Daniel’s asks:

- Residency pinning: supported. We can map regional shards to us-west-2 for CA traffic and us-east-1 for east coast. This is a routing policy on the smart routing layer plus dedicated model clusters in the chosen region.
- Retention: we currently support flexible retention per data-class via per-customer config. Defaults: logs 365d (w/ export), transcripts 90d, embeddings 180d. We can expose TTLs in the console and enforce via policy. If Skyline wants shorter retention we can set that on their tenant config.
- Support access / break-glass: recommend the following implementation to satisfy their controls:
  * Break-glass requires Jira ticket + one on-call approver (Redwood) + one customer approver OR a pre-authorized emergency roster.
  * Access is time-limited, role-bound, and all actions are logged to immutable audit logs (write-once S3 w/ retention policy).
  * Session recording: we can capture console sessions and record API calls (x-request-id + full request/response metadata redacted by policy).
  * KMS: customer-managed keys supported for private; hosted customers can use Redwood-managed KMS with HSM-backed keys on request.

Monica — can you produce a minimal RBAC matrix for the meeting on Wed (30-min) that maps Skyline personas (admin, support-tech, auditor) to Redwood roles (tenant-admin, support-1, support-2, observer)? That will make the canary MPA appendix more concrete.

Irene — suggest proposing Wed 12/15 at 10:00AM PST to Daniel for the technical sync.

-Aditya
Sr. Security Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Daniel Reed <daniel.reed@skylinehealth.com>, Lena Park <lena.park@skylinehealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Follow-up: data handling, residency, and support access requirements for Skyline Health

Hi Daniel / Lena —

Thanks — this is all helpful. Proposed outcomes and next steps:

1) Technical sync (30 min) — Wed 15 Dec, 10:00AM PST — confirm regional pinning, retention TTLs, and break-glass flow. Monica and Aditya will join to go over the RBAC matrix and audit/tracing capabilities.
2) We’ll update the privacy appendix to show: US-only residency with CA traffic pinned to us-west-2, transcripts 90d, embeddings 180d, logs 365d (configurable).
3) Break-glass: draft flow will require Jira SUP ticket + Redwood on-call + customer security approver; session recording + immutable audit logs to be included in the appendix.
4) Deliverables by Fri 12/18: updated MPA appendix (Irene), RBAC matrix (Monica), and a short diagram of the break-glass flow (Aditya). I’ll share the DocuSign link once legal reviews the appendix.

If that timeline works, I’ll schedule Wed’s sync and share a short agenda.

Appreciate the quick turnaround —
Irene Choi
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
